raw_response:
I farm only 10.9 mu, so I cannot take big risks. What feeds my family is the wheat-maize rotation, and with some people working off-farm, I mostly depend on steady harvest, not fancy changes. I will do mostly what worked before. Around here everyone puts in wheat first in October, then maize right after wheat harvest in June. If I spend too much on fertilizer and chemicals, cash gets tight, but if I cut too much and the crop turns weak, that hurts more. So I will use moderate fertilizer, keep the field clean, and use the well mainly at the important stages.

For wheat, I will sow in early October with a common improved variety people nearby use, not the most expensive seed. I usually put base fertilizer before sowing, then look at the wheat in spring. If the leaves are pale or growth is weak, I topdress once at jointing. Wheat needs water more surely, so I plan a few irrigations if rain is not enough. After harvest, the time is tight, so for maize I will not do heavy tillage. I will clear the wheat, make a quick seedbed, and plant maize fast like my neighbors do. Maize grows well after wheat here, so I will still feed it, but a bit less carefully than wheat because summer rain can help. If insects or weeds show up, I spray, otherwise I do not waste money.
